text:
maria: noticing a weird perf cliff on prod yesterday around 17:10 UTC. tail latency for short requests (<=32 tokens) jumped from 25ms -> 120ms for ~3m. traces show a lot of kernel swaps and cuda kernel launch stalls.

jonathan: yup saw the same in logs. looks like when short and long seqs interleave we oscillate between two kernel configs and both warmup caches repeatedly.

alex: can you paste the probe logs? was this during a rollout?

maria: not a rollout. here's a condensed probe snippet from device-9: 
```
PROBE start seq=16 kernel=K_small warmup_ms=12
PROBE start seq=512 kernel=K_long warmup_ms=210
K_small evict kv_cache tenant=team-x
K_long evict kv_cache tenant=team-y
K_small launch delay=88ms
```
noticed evictions of prefix/KV between kernel switches.

kim: that sounds like cache thrash + kernel churn. two ideas: (A) sticky-kernel policy (stick to last kernel for N seconds unless throughput drops) or (B) per-device tenant affinity so KV/cache isn't tossed when a different tenant's long seqs run.

jonathan: sticky-kernel makes sense but we risk suboptimal perf for long sequences if we wrongly stick. need heuristics to detect "churn" vs genuine shift in workload.

alex: proposal: a churn score = weighted moving average of kernel-switch events per minute. if churn_score > T then enable sticky for Xs, but only for same tenant or same model-variant. Also only sticky if latency for current bucket is below SLA.

maria: +1. also think we should prefer microbatching for short seqs when there's capacity — reduces kernel switches since multiple shorts can be fused into same kernel path. We already have a microbatch window param. maybe auto-increase it for churny periods.

kim: combine both: sticky-kernel + adaptive microbatch. And add a cache-protect mode: mark recent KV entries as protected for Yms to avoid evict on kernel swap. cheap: change LRU window for protected keys.

jonathan: edge cases: memory pressure and multi-tenant fairness. can't let one tenant protect everything. protect policy should be per-tenant token-volume cap.

maria: agree. let's draft a minimal config that the tuner can apply dynamically: 
```json
{
  "sticky_kernel": {"enabled": true, "duration_ms": 5000, "min_throughput_drop_pct": 0},
  "churn_detector": {"window_s": 60, "switches_threshold": 10},
  "adaptive_microbatch": {"enabled": true, "max_window_ms": 20, "min_batch_size": 4},
  "kv_protect": {"enabled": true, "protect_ms": 3000, "tenant_token_cap": 20000}
}
```

alex: looks good for an experiment. we should A/B on a subset of devices (canary 10%) and measure tail p50/p95, kernel_switch_rate, and mem pressure. ops-bot can create the canary?

ops-bot: canary created: autotune-canary-1995, devices=58, start=now. metrics dashboard: link https://dash.internal/redwood/canaries/1995

jonathan: also add a metric "kv-eviction-rate" per tenant. want to make sure we don't silently punish team-y.

maria: action items: (1) implement churn_detector + sticky enforcement (jonathan) (2) adaptive microbatch tweak (alex) (3) kv_protect LRU flag + tenant cap (kim) (4) run canary + collect kernel_switch_rate, kv_eviction_rate, latency percentiles (maria)

kim: timeline? can we ship an experiment by EOW?

jonathan: I can PR churn_detector today, test tomorrow. alex/kim good to iterate in parallel.

maria: awesome. thanks all. i'll check canary after 1h and post preliminary numbers. :thumbsup:
